entries.title: Terms in Skim open their glossary card
entries.body: In Skim, the terms listed under a stop open the same card the Glossary uses: point at one, move to it with the keyboard, or tap it on a touch screen to keep it open. On your own articles the card lets you hide a term, and where the Glossary is available it opens that too.

entries.title: New Skim routes are asked for fuller cues
entries.body: On newly made Skim routes, the AI is asked to write the cue before each quote as complete sentences. Where a quote leans on words it does not explain, it is asked to give the question or the options first, but only when the article's material supports that. Routes already made keep their cues until they are made again.

entries.title: Features page shows Learn's current tabs
entries.body: The Learn and Quiz pictures on the features page were taken before Remember was renamed Learn. They now show the Recall, Tutorial, Explore and Quiz tabs as they appear in the app.

entries.title: Switching accounts no longer mixes two readers' work
entries.body: If the signed-in account changed while a page was open, say from another tab, the second account could see what the first had typed on the add-an-article page, and a late save could go out under the wrong account. The add page now stops, such saves are refused, and unsent chat and Feedback drafts are dropped.

entries.title: Chat previews show plain words, not markup
entries.body: The one-line preview of a chat's latest answer, shown under a Debate claim, a Glossary entry or a Citations row and on the collapsed chat card, used the raw first line of the answer, so asterisks and passage reference codes showed in it. It now shows the answer's opening words as plain text.

entries.title: Access & sharing no longer warns while checking
entries.body: On an article's Metadata page, Access & sharing said it could not check on every load, before the check had finished, and one failed check left that message up until you reloaded. It now says "Checking who can read this…" during the first check and tries again by itself after a failure; the failure message stays until a check succeeds.

entries.title: Another kind of bot-check page is recognised
entries.body: Some sites answer with a page that checks you are not a bot instead of the article. One form of that page was not recognised when you added an article, so it was taken in as if it were the article. The app now recognises it, refuses it and says so; it does not get past the bot check.
